hints: Focus on reversing addition polymerisation by putting the C=C double bond back between the two carbons in the repeat unit.
Count the carbons in each repeat unit first, polymer K has 4 carbons so it must come from a butene, and polymer J has 5 carbons so it must come from a pentene.
Look at where the side chains sit, since both carbons in each repeat unit carry an alkyl group, the double bond must have been in the middle of the monomer chain.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the polymer type**

Both polymers have only C and H in a saturated carbon chain repeat unit. This is classic addition polymerisation of an alkene, where the C=C opens to form two new C-C single bonds.

To find the monomer, reverse this: $$-\text{CH(R)-CH(R')}- \rightarrow \text{R-CH=CH-R'}$$

**Find the monomer for polymer K**

Polymer K is $-[\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CH(CH}_3)]-$. Joining the two CH carbons with a double bond gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$.

This is a 4-carbon chain with the double bond starting at carbon 2. That is but-2-ene.

**Find the monomer for polymer J**

Polymer J is $-[\text{CH(C}_2\text{H}_5)\text{CH(CH}_3)]-$. Joining the two CH carbons with a double bond gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CHCH}_3$.

This is a 5-carbon chain with the double bond starting at carbon 2. That is pent-2-ene.

**Match to the table**

Polymer J is from pent-2-ene and polymer K is from but-2-ene. That combination matches the correct row.

options.A: Incorrect. Pent-1-ene is $\text{CH}_2\text{=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and would give $-[\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)]-$, not the J repeat unit. But-1-ene is $\text{CH}_2\text{=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and would give $-[\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_2\text{CH}_3)]-$, not the K repeat unit.
options.B: Incorrect. Polymer K is correctly from but-2-ene, but polymer J is not from pent-1-ene. Pent-1-ene has a terminal $\text{CH}_2=$ group, so one carbon in the repeat unit would be unsubstituted $\text{CH}_2$, whereas J has both carbons substituted.
options.C: Incorrect. Polymer J is correctly from pent-2-ene, but polymer K is not from but-1-ene. But-1-ene has a terminal $\text{CH}_2=$ group, so it would give one $\text{CH}_2$ group in the repeat unit, whereas K has $\text{CH(CH}_3)$ on both sides.
options.D: Correct. But-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_3$, opens to give $-[\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CH(CH}_3)]-$, which is polymer K. Pent-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CHCH}_3$, opens to give $-[\text{CH(CH}_2\text{CH}_3)\text{CH(CH}_3)]-$, which is polymer J.
